title: Points for Plastic: Wecyclers Takes Cargo Bikes into Lagos Streets
conflicts: Households and jobs differ by date and source (5,000 and about 30 staff, AFP Feb 2014; 5,000+ and 52, Lionesses Jan 2015; 7,000 and 75, MIT; 10,000+ and 100+, D+C undated): only the dated AFP figures and VOA's 2015 description are used. Vehicles: cargo bicycles (D+C, AFP, Echoing Green) vs tricycles (True Africa, Al Jazeera): cargo bicycles used, as the founder described them. King Baudouin prize dated 2018/19 (The Benchmark) and 'recent' in April 2019 (Al Jazeera): story says 2019.
notes: Co-founders are not named because only a surname (Fallon, via MIT) was found. The story ends with Wecyclers still small and unprofitable in 2015 rather than a success claim. Her later move into Lagos State government (The Benchmark) is left out for want of a second source. Guardian Nigeria, Engineering for Change, BET and Tony Elumelu Foundation pages do not load for the verifier. Stance affirms (William James, Talks to Teachers ch. X).
